Consider this imaginary causal system and answer yes or no.
The only causal links in this toy model are these: Whether the ferry runs on the winter timetable and whether the crossing is delayed both affect whether passengers file a complaint; whether the ferry runs on the winter timetable and whether the crossing is delayed do not affect each other. No other influences exist. Overall, the probability that the ferry runs on the winter timetable is 55%. Overall, the probability that the crossing is delayed is 80%. Whenever winter timetable and delayed crossing, the probability that passengers file a complaint is 45%. Whenever winter timetable and on-time crossing, the probability that passengers file a complaint is 45%. Whenever summer timetable and delayed crossing, the probability that passengers file a complaint is 95%. Whenever summer timetable and on-time crossing, the probability that passengers file a complaint is 45%.

Looking only at cases where complaint filed, is it more likely that the crossing is delayed when winter timetable than when summer timetable?

Below is a small causal model with three yes/no variables. Use only the model to answer the question.

Whenever town hotel, the probability that guests book half board is 50%. Whenever beach hotel and half board, the probability that guests leave a five-star review is 80%. Whenever town hotel and room only, the probability that guests leave a five-star review is 25%.

If an outside intervention made it true everywhere that the hotel is near the beach, would it be more likely that guests leave a five-star review than if the intervention ruled this out?
